articles.title: Maybe it’s a new tagline. Maybe it’s more punctuation. Maybelline’s 35-year-old slogan has an update
articles.summary: First introduced in 1991, ‘Maybe she’s born with it’ is out the door – but is the new slogan a glow-up? Alyx, I hear a certain makeup brand has updated its tagline. Why is this a big deal?
body: The jingle that has been burned into the minds of women around the world since its Christy Turlington-helmed debut in 1991, “Maybe she’s born with it, maybe it’s Maybelline”, has received what has being described as a “modernisation”. In a new campaign with Miley Cyrus, the “she’s” will be replaced with “we’re”, which both changes the observer’s perspective to something a little more self-directed and makes it more inclusive. But it’s a punctuation change that is raising eyebrows.
Replacing “she” with “we” feels like a positive move. So what’s turning heads?
They’ve replaced a single comma with a pair of full stops. The slogan is now: “Maybe. We’re born with it. Maybe. It’s Maybelline.”

Not according to Sandrine Jolly, global brand president of Maybelline New York. She told WWD that, previously, “the jingle was giving ambiguity – it was more of a question”. Now: “The ‘maybe’ is not a doubt or a hesitation any more. ‘Maybe’, period, is a statement of possibility, and that is what we want to be for women.”
points: First introduced in 1991, ‘Maybe she’s born with it’ is out the door – but is the new slogan a glow-up?

articles.summary: The best non-stick pan we’ve reviewed is on sale this week, along with some other great non-toxic kitchen deals we have tested and recommend. Welcome to Worth it, where Filter editors spotlight one genuinely good discount on something we have tested and loved.
body: At the Filter, we’re on a mission to reduce microplastics and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (Pfas) in our kitchens. It is a gradual process, but even small amounts of some Pfas are unsafe to consume. And though we don’t entirely know how bad microplastics are for our health, their growing prevalence everywhere ( even the soil ) is causing concern.

This past year we have tested plastic-free cutting boards, non-toxic pans, food storage containers and other kitchen tools to help you make well-informed decisions. Items free of Pfas and microplastics are investments, so we like to spotlight good deals when we find them. This week, we’re sharing two non-toxic cookware discounts worth a look. Both ranked highly in our testing.
After testing 13 non-toxic pans, Our Place’s Titanium Always Pan Pro emerged as our “best overall” winner.

“It heated up quickly, eggs slid off the pan smoothly, and proteins got an even sear despite the micro-dot ridges on the pan’s surface (that help with the non-stick effect),” write the scientists at Drexel’s Food Lab.

articles.title: I have noticed a pattern with product ratings that could lead to biased reviews. Is it legal?
articles.summary: The practice you’ve noticed is colloquially known as ‘review gating’, writes consumer affairs and policy professional Kat George. And no, it isn’t legal. I have noticed that when I get an email inviting me to review a product or service I have purchased online or physically, if I select a high…
body: Kat says: Screening reviews and sorting feedback based on a consumer’s initial sentiment is known colloquially online as “review gating”. It’s a dark pattern that is common enough that Google has banned it outright. And while the Australian consumer law doesn’t name the practice explicitly, it is clearly prohibited under laws relating to business reviews and false and misleading practices.

In early 2026, Google made some pointed changes to its Maps User Generated Content policy. The new policy states that Google does not allow businesses to “discourage or prohibit negative reviews, or selectively solicit positive reviews from customers”. What you have described sounds like businesses doing both of those things.

Google also has real consequences for businesses that are found to be in breach of its policy, so your experience is worth reporting directly to Google. Penalties include removing reviews that breach the policy, placing restrictions and alerts on business profiles, limiting the business’s eligibility to receive new reviews and temporarily hiding historical reviews.

articles.title: Ariana Grande’s Flipped Bob Is Fall’s Sweetest Trend
articles.summary: “After being blonde for so long, her ends were ready to go,” hairstylist Brandon Pietsch says about the chop, adding that they cut off about six inches. “Retro looks are coming back for fall in full force.”
body: Late last month, Ariana Grande sent shockwaves around the beauty world with a single selfie. The singer, actor, and beauty brand founder had recently gone back to brunette, officially ending her Wicked era. Now, she took it a step further by chopping off her hair.

Grande isn’t the only celebrity going in on the flipped-out bob. Margot Robbie styled her hair in a similar way—with a return of the side bang!—for the Chanel Cruise show that took place in Australia on November 5th. The look, done by her go-to hairstylist Bryce Scarlett, was a sweet take on her somewhat-new blunt bob (and that cut came hot on the heels of the end of her Wuthering Heights tour, are we starting to see a pattern?). French girl extraordinaire Lea Seydoux and Ayo Edebiri have also taken their hair to new degrees with flipped ends.

articles.title: Model Caroline Trentini Reflects of Her Much-Memed Shoot With Iowa’s Governor-to-Be Rob Sand and Steven Meisel
articles.summary: “I remember everything, the smells, the atmosphere, the music,” says model Caroline Trentini of her first Steven Meisel shoot, which happened to feature a future governor-to-be.
body: One day in the early 2000s at Pier 59 Studios, Steven Meisel gathered a cast of young, up-and-coming models that included Lisa Cant, Diana Dondoe, Caroline Trentini, and Iowa native and then-college student Rob Sand. Brana Wolf styled, Garren was on hair, and Dame Pat McGrath painted the makeup. Grungy styles from Helmut Lang, Prada, and Gucci were on the racks. Titled “Be My Baby,” the shoot explored the renaissance of punkish adolescence on the runways, and while the spread originally appeared in the February 2004 pages of Vogue Italia, over two decades later, the shoot’s legacy has taken on a completely new life.

Last week, we connected the dots that Iowa Governor-Elect Rob Sand was once a high fashion model, walking the runways for brands including Prada and Japanese cult label Number Nine (a recent photo has since circulated of him sporting a sweatshirt from the show that he walked in 2004). Following our post, he took to Instagram with images from “Be My Baby,” with the caption, “I’m disappointed to learn images of me modeling for Prada are circulating. Because this shot from Italian Vogue is much better.”

articles.title: High-Protein Packaged Foods May Not Be As Healthy As They Look
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Of the three major macronutrients—protein, carbs, and fat—protein has the best reputation, and it’s fairly well deserved. We need significant amounts of protein in our diet, and nothing particularly bad happens if we get too much.
body: Take a close look here—sometimes a food will boast of a certain amount of protein per package but the package contains two or three servings. Other times, the protein per serving is correct, and we're supposed to be excited to have, say, 7 grams per serving. That's just not very much—and certainly not worth paying extra or choosing a less-delicious food just for those few added grams.

It’s good to know how much protein you need in your diet. If you’re not gaining or losing weight, and not doing very much exercise, a 150-pound person only needs about 54 grams of protein a day. (I've done the math for various body weights here.) If you’re working out a lot, or if you’re trying to gain or lose weight (yep, either way), that same 150-pound person will need more like 81 to 95 grams of protein per day. More is OK, but not necessary.

So if you’re trying to get 90 grams per day, 30 grams per meal is a reasonable amount to shoot for. Coincidentally, 30 grams is the amount of protein that tends to make a meal feel satisfying. You can do the math to figure out whether a protein-added product is going to be helpful in your day’s diet.

When experiencing a five-course tasting menu ($145), I wasn’t expecting toast to be a main attraction. But even with competition from luxurious courses featuring everything from a complex Hokkaido scallop to an assertive charred rib-eye with peaches, All Well ’s puffed grain toast left a lasting impression.

After three years at two-Michelin-starred Oriole, Larry Feldmeier partnered with Noah Sandoval, fellow Oriole alum and James Beard winner for Best Chef: Great Lakes, to open the ambitious West Loop restaurant All Well, which offers both a la carte bar options and the aforementioned tasting; the toast is only available as part of the latter experience.

articles.summary: Each of the chefs featured in our new national Chef of the Year category made news in a major way. But their most recent projects are just one part of their story.

San Francisco diners became acquainted with powerhouse couple Laura and Sayat Ozyilmaz through their championing of Eastern Mediterranean cuisine at Dalida. That restaurant told the story of Sayat’s upbringing and influences in Istanbul, Turkey, opening in 2023 inside a historic building within the lush environs of the Presidio and earning critical acclaim for the duo’s cooking.

In the years since, diners came to know Laura outside of Dalida. She completed an impressive run on Top Chef in 2024, where viewers saw her deftly plant one foot in Mediterranean food and another in Mexican cuisine, showcasing her skill in both fields throughout the season. With the 2026 debut of the Ozyilmazes’ restaurant Maria Isabel, the food feels like an even fuller expression of Laura’s heritage and personal history.

articles.title: You’re Going to Want to Keep an Eye on Eldar Isgandarov
articles.summary: The young Azerbaijani actor makes a wonderful splash in two of the year’s best films.
body: Last month, Eldar Isgandarov attended Julio Torres’s Halloween party dressed as Candace, co-owner of the radical feminist bookstore Women & Women First on the sketch comedy series Portlandia. This was an important place to begin our conversation: Isgandarov wanted to explain why his halo of brown curls was a bit mussed. The night prior, he’d donned a wig cap and a long blond wig. He tried to stick close to his friend—who went as Candace’s partner, Toni—throughout the night. “If you separate, it gets tricky,” he says. Otherwise, “they’d think she’s Velma and I’m Lucius Malfoy.”
points: The young Azerbaijani actor makes a wonderful splash in two of the year’s best films.
